 Dated:- This the 1st day of October 2024  M.V.C. NO. 6142/2023 Petitioner/s:
1. Smt.Lakshmi W/o. Munireddy,
Aged about 47 years.
2. Sri Munireddy S/o. Munivenkatappa Aged about 51 years.

Both are R/at:
No.365, 3rd Cross,
Sriramachandrapura Arehalli Badamanavarthekaval,

(By Sri. M.J. Amarnatha Advocate)
 V/s  2  SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 Respondent:
Sri Omkar Kamalaksha Kini S/o Kamalaksha Gopal Kini No.PL 5B/10 Sector-14, Khanda Colony, Panvel Raigad, Panvel,

1 (RC owner of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. MH-46-AT-2889)
(By Sri Lakshmeesha Advocate)
 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Chandra Shekar M., who met with road traffic accident.
2. The petitioner no.1 is the mother and petitioner no.2 is the father of deceased by name Chandra Shekar M.

That on 31.03.2023 at about 08.15 p.m., while the deceased was proceeding in his Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-ED-7585 on the extreme left side of the Road on Uttarahalli Main Road, Bengaluru and when he reached in front of RR Plywood, at that time the rider of Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.MH-46-AT-2889 rode his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner with high speed dashed to the motor cycle of the deceased and caused SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 the accident, result of which the deceased sustained grievous fatal injuries all over his body.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to BGS Hospital for treatment wherein he took initial treatment and further had taken treatment at Leelavathi Hospital, KIMS Hospital and finally he was admitted to Sparsha Hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient.
But in spite of best treatment given by the doctors, he succumbed to the injuries while under treatment in Sparsha Hospital on 02-04-2023.
Later on Post Mortem was conducted at Victoria Hospital and then handed over the body to the petitioners.

The petitioners have spent around Rs.3,00,000/- towards Hospital charges, treatment, medicines, and transportation of dead body, cremation, funeral,
obsequies and other death related ceremonies.
2(a). Prior to the accident, the deceased Chandra Shekar M., was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 16 years and he was student.
Due to the sudden demise of deceased, the petitioners have sustained mental agony and great financial inconvenience.
Hence, respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

The respondent- Omkar Kamalaksha Kini, the Owner of Motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.MH-46-AT-2889 has filed written statement and contended that the alleged accident occurred due to unskilled and un- licensed minor who rode the Motorcycle belong to the petitioner No.2.
The deceased was minor and had no driving license and he had no knowledge of driving the motorcycle.
The riding of the Motorcycle by deceased minor itself is an illegal act.
The respondent is not responsible for the accident.

The respondent further contended that in CC No.4991/2023, the petitioner no.2 is arrayed as accused no.2 for the offence under column -5(1) 180 of IMV Act pending before II MMTC, at Bengaluru for disposal.
Hence, respondent is not liable to pay any damages to the petitioners as claimed by them.

2 4.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove

that, Chandra Shekar M was died on account of road traffic accident on 31-03-2023 at about 8.15 p.m. in front of RR Playwood, Uttarahalli Main Road towards Uttarahalli, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.MH-46-AT- 2889?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3

. What Order or Award?
5.
The petitioner No.2 got examined himself as Pw1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P.10.
On the other hand the respondent got examined himself as RW.1 but not got marked any documents.

6. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and learned counsel for respondent.
7.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative Issue No.2 - Partly in the Affirmative Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 8. Issue No.1: Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident, the deceased while was proceeding in his Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-ED-7585 on the extreme left side of the Road on Uttarahalli Main Road, Bengaluru and when he SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 reached in front of RR Plywood, at that time the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.MH-46-AT-2889 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) rode his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner with high speed dashed to the motor cycle of the deceased and caused the accident, result of which the deceased sustained grievous fatal injuries all over his body.
But in spite of best treatment, he succumbed to the injuries while w taking treatment in Sparsha Hospital on 02-04-2023.

9. In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.2 who is the father of deceased got examined himself as Pw1 and produced in all 10 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.8 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Inquest mahazar, PM report, u/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon and charge sheet are the material documents to prove the present issue.
Lakshmi vs Omkar Kamalaksha Kini on 1 October, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121032979/
3 10.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Munireddy who is father of deceased, case has been registered against the rider of the offending vehicle in Crime No 0129/2023 of Kengeri Trafffi Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 IPC.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle and SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 owner/petitioner no.2 of the motorcycle bearing No.MH- 46-AT-2889 for the offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC & u/Sec.146, 198 IMV Act and Sec. 5(1) 180 of MV Act.

11. So far as the rash and negligent act on the part of the respondent who is the owner cum rider of the offending vehicle is concerned, it is not in dispute that at the time of accident deceased was riding his motorcycle from Kengeri side towards Uttarahalli and offending vehicle which was coming from opposite direction i.e., from Uttarahalli towards Kengeri while taking right turn at the spot of accident hit against the motor cycle of the deceased .
The accident in question has occurred in Kengeri -Uttarahalli road.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 30 feet and the accident in question has occurred on the left side of Kengeri- Uttarahalli road.
The respondent who was riding his vehicle on the right side of Uttarahalli -Kengeri road, at the spot of accident took right turn of the vehicle.

When respondent was taking right turn he ought to have taken all kind of precautions by seeing whether any vehicles are coming from opposite direction and whether road is clear to take right turn of his vehicle.
From the spot SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 mahazar and sketch it can be said that the deceased was proceeding on the correct direction of the road.

12. It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that at the time of accident deceased was minor and he was not holding driving license, hence because of the illegal act of the minor riding the vehicle without holding license the accident in question has occurred, hence, they are not liable to pay the compensation.
13. In the light of the contention taken by the respondent, if the materials placed on record are perused, it is not in dispute that the deceased was aged about 16 years at the time of accident.
As he was 16 years old it can be said that he was not holding driving license.
The petitioner no.2 is the RC owner of the vehicle driven by the deceased.
As petitioner no.2 has permitted the minor to ride the vehicle, charge sheet has been registered against the petitioner no.2 for the offence punishable u/Sec.5 (1) 180 of MV Act.

Admittedly, no abated charge sheet has been filed against the minor and there is no allegation in the charge sheet against the minor of his riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and caused for the accident.
Even this court has also observed that SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 the minor was proceeding on the correct direction of the road.
Had the respondent ride his vehicle on the correct direction of the road and had he taken precautionary measures while taking right turn this accident could have been avoided.
Merely because deceased who was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-ED-7585 was minor, on that ground alone it cannot be said that minor has also contributed negligence.
For the act of petitioner no.2 permitted his minor son to ride the motorcycle, he was prosecuted for the offence punishable u/Sec. 5(1) 180 of MV Act and he is facing the trail.
Hence, it can be said that respondent alone is held liable for the accident.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

Lakshmi vs Omkar Kamalaksha Kini on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121032979/
4 14.
Issue no 2 :
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned respective counsels, it can be said that the deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
In the Ex.P10 - Aadhar card the date of birth of deceased is shown as 17-04-2007.
Hence it can be gathered that as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 16 years.
15. As per the case of petitioners, deceased was a student pursuing his studies but they have not produced SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 any educational document of the deceased.
If Ex.P.10/Aadhar card is perused, as on the date of accident the deceased was a minor aged about 16 years.
The accident in question has occurred in the month of March -2023.

If the accident has not occurred and if the injured has not succumbed to the injuries and if injured Chandra Shekar was survived, within few years he would have completed his education and would have secured job suitable to his qualification, would have earned income and would have maintained his parents/family.
16. Now the quantum of compensation needs to be considered.

In the case of 'KISHAN GOPAL AND ANR. VS. LALA AND ORS.' rendered by Division Bench of Hon'ble Supreme court (2014) I SCC 244,
by referring the calculation made in Lata Wadhwa and Others/State of Bihar and Ors where in while examining the tortuous liability of the tort -feasor has examined the criteria for awarding compensation for death of children in accident between age group of 10 to 15 years awarding compensation taking the contribution of the children to the family at Rs.15,000/- p.a by applying 11 as multiplier, it was held that, the rupee value has come down drastically from the year 1994 when the notional income of the non earning prior to the date of the accident was fixed at Rs.15,000/-

entities.text: KISHAN GOPAL AND ANR. VS. LALA AND ORS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa and Others/State of Bihar and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the deceased SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 boy had he been alive would have certainly contributed substantially to the family by working hard.

In the said case by considering all the reason it had taken the notional income of the deceased boy who was aged about 10 years as Rs.30,000/- and by applying legal principle laid down in sarala Varma case the multiplier of 15 has been applied.
Thus Rs.4,50,000/- was awarded as loss of dependency apart from other heads.

17. Further in MFA No 4867 of 2020 (MV ) between Lakshmi @ Lakshmi Bail and another / The Managing Director BMTC decided on 29th day of November 2023 the boy aged about 16 years studying in I PUC met with an accident during the year 2018 and succumbed to the injuries.
In the said case the hon'ble High court has taken the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.9,000/- p.m.
To the aforesaid income 40% is added towards future prospects and 18 multiplier is applied as deceased was aged about 16 years.

18. Further in Chetana and others / Babuji M and Others reported in 2021 ACJ 1146 the Hon'ble Division Bnch has observed that that "there is no prohibition under the child and Adolescent Labour (prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 that the SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 adolescent of 17 years to involve milk vending business.

entities.text: Chetana and others / Babuji M and Others reported in 2021 ACJ 1146
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: child and Adolescent Labour (prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The division bench considering the said Act has assessed the notional income and also awarded the future prospects.
19. Coming to the case in hand at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 16 years.

If the observation made in the aforesaid judgment is applied to the case in hand, when in a case of death of boy aged about 17 years the Hon'ble High Court of Division Bench has assessed notional income of Lakshmi vs Omkar Kamalaksha Kini on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121032979/
5

the deceased and 40% future prospect is added to the said income and when in MFA No.4067/2020,
the Hon'ble High Court has assessed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.9,000/- per month who was aged about 16 years at the time of accident which was occurred in the year 2018, under such circumstances it is reasonable to assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month.

20. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the deceased having considered by this tribunal as Rs.11,000/- p.m, on which 40% is added towards the future prospect which comes to Rs.15,400/-.
Out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 Rs.7,700/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is 18 for the age of the deceased.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.16,63,200/- (7,700 x 12 x 18).
21. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 and 2 have lost their son.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/-
and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30 th October 2017.

22. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.
SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.
SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/- towards loss of estate.

23. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/- 2 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/- funeral expenses 3 Loss of filial consortium Rs. 96,800/-
(Rs.48,400x2) 4 Loss of dependency Rs.16,63,200/-

Lakshmi vs Omkar Kamalaksha Kini on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121032979/
6

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.17,96,300/- (Rupees Seventeen Lakh Ninety Six Thousand Three Hundred Only) and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.1, the offending vehicle was not having insurance policy.
The respondent/owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 1 to 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,96,300/-(Rupees Seventeen Lakh Ninety Six Thousand Three Hundred Only) with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the amount along with interest within 2 months from the date of award.

SCCH-24 M.V.C.6142 of 2023 Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.11,96,300/- Petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs 6,00,000/-
Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 2 shall be deposited in their names in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
